title: Hyper slowness issue
body: I'm transferring three flight-information URLs with curl on Windows 10. With a build using `-DUSE_HYPER`, the command takes at least a minute, with long pauses between URLs, whether the URLs come from a config file or the command line and whether or not I use `--parallel`. The curl bundled with Windows completes the same three requests in under a second. My build is curl 8.2.0-DEV with Hyper 1.0.0-rc.3.

symptoms_visible: My curl build with `-DUSE_HYPER` takes at least a minute to fetch three small HTTPS URLs, with long pauses between them.
The same requests finish in under a second with the curl bundled with Windows; `--parallel` does not remove the pauses.
N0.label: N0 Hyper transfers reported extremely slow

symptoms_visible: The long pauses remain after updating Rust, pulling Hyper master, and rebuilding everything.
I can also reproduce the roughly one-minute runtime with a curl-plus-Hyper build on Linux.
N1.label: N1 current dependencies and cross-platform reproduction confirmed

symptoms_visible: After rebuilding with the proposed changes, the three-URL command still takes about 61 seconds instead of about 1.5 seconds with the Windows curl.
In some runs I receive only two of the three responses.
N2_x.label: N2_x initial Hyper polling patch aftermath

symptoms_visible: The first response arrives immediately, followed by pauses of about 30 seconds before the later responses.
Forcing HTTP/1.1 makes the same three requests complete in about 300 milliseconds.
N2.label: N2 protocol trace and packet evidence collected

symptoms_visible: I've rebuilt curl and Hyper from current git master containing the change; I haven't re-run my three-URL benchmark yet.
N3.label: N3 rebuilt with fix, unverified

symptoms_visible: The rebuilt curl finishes my three-URL script in about a second — the minute-long pauses are gone (the Windows-bundled curl remains somewhat faster).
N_terminal.label: terminal Hyper minute-long stalls resolved

question_patterns: Can this be reproduced with a curl-plus-Hyper build on another platform?
Is the delay specific to your Windows and Schannel build?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: I can reproduce it on Linux too. Normal curl takes one or two seconds, while curl with Hyper takes about a minute for the same three URLs.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: I cannot reproduce it outside this Windows Schannel build; the Hyper build is fast on Linux and with the other TLS backends.
It reproduces on Linux as well, but the complete run takes about 55 seconds rather than exactly one minute.

edges.comment: The reporter independently added that updating Rust, pulling Hyper master, and rebuilding did not change the result. A second affected user's Linux reproduction is folded into the simulated user side.

solution.intent: Apply the initial Hyper polling and wake-handling changes from PR #11344 to make completed Hyper tasks available without waiting for a later transfer-loop poll.
solution.concrete_example: Build curl with PR #11344, which adjusts the Hyper polling path after observations that a second immediate `hyper_executor_poll()` could return the response.

edges.comment: PR #11344 made the test fast for one contributor, but it did not resolve the reporter's case. A later current-master test still took 61.321 seconds and sometimes returned only two responses.

question_patterns: Can you capture a timestamped curl trace showing what happens during each pause?
Please trace the three transfers and report whether curl opens a new connection during the 30-second waits.
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: The first response arrives quickly. Then `Curl_hyper_stream` is called about once per second with `select_res` 0 for roughly 30 seconds before activity resumes, and the same thing happens before the third response. The trace does not show a new connection during those pauses.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: The trace shows a DNS lookup and a new TCP/TLS connection being created for each URL, and those connection attempts consume the 30 seconds.
The same idle pattern appears, but the pauses are around 28 seconds instead of exactly 30.

question_patterns: Can you inspect the HTTP/2 traffic with Wireshark and an SSLKEYLOGFILE?
What frames does normal curl send compared with the Hyper backend for the three requests?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: In my decrypted capture, normal curl sends one HTTP/2 connection preface, settings/window update, and then requests 1, 2, and 3. The Hyper build sends a connection preface and settings/window update before request 1, then another preface and settings/window update before request 2, and again before request 3.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: Both builds send exactly one HTTP/2 connection preface followed by all three request streams; the captures are identical until the response data.
The Hyper capture has the same repeated prefaces, but the window-update frame ordering differs slightly.

question_patterns: Please compare the default Hyper protocol negotiation with an explicitly HTTP/1.1 run.
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: Yes. The default Hyper run takes more than 60 seconds for this endpoint, while `curl --http1.1` completes the same three URLs in about 300 milliseconds.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: Forcing HTTP/1.1 still takes more than a minute and has the same two long pauses.

edges.comment: Trace, protocol comparison, and packet-capture observations came from multiple technical contributors and affected users, folded into one simulated user side. The answers contain raw timings, calls, and frame sequences; identifying the lifecycle defect is engineer-side inference.

solution.intent: Disable HTTP/2 in curl's Hyper integration and use HTTP/1.1 as the safe temporary path, because curl creates a Hyper client connection per request and sends a new HTTP/2 connection preface on an already reused connection; restoring Hyper HTTP/2 requires connection-scoped lifecycle integration.
solution.concrete_example: Apply PR #12191 so Hyper-backed transfers negotiate HTTP/1.1 instead of the broken HTTP/2 path. The existing integration creates a `hyper_clientconn` for each request, causing repeated HTTP/2 prefaces and server GOAWAY/error handling; proper HTTP/2 support should return only after the Hyper client/executor lifecycle is redesigned around connections and multiplexed transfers.
solution.inference_hint: The packet capture supplies only the repeated frame sequence. Engineers inferred that curl was creating a `hyper_clientconn` per request, making the repeated prefaces invalid on the reused HTTP/2 connection, and that server GOAWAY/error handling led to delayed retries or dropped requests. The reporter's fast `--http1.1` and post-PR measurements validate disabling Hyper HTTP/2, but do not themselves name that internal lifecycle cause.

edges.comment: Reshaped per round-3 audit: the fix (disable HTTP/2 for the Hyper backend, #12191) is proposed here on the pre-fix diagnostic evidence; the rebuild benchmark moves terminal-side as verification.

question_patterns: Could you rebuild curl and Hyper from current git master and re-run your three-URL benchmark?
Please update to the latest master, rebuild, and tell me what times you see for the same three transfers.
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: Rebuilt from current master and re-ran my three-URL script (responses discarded to NUL): much better — 1.137s vs 0.233s for the Windows-bundled curl, and a later run 0.974s vs 0.803s. No more minute-long pauses.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: The rebuilt master still takes about 61 seconds and sometimes returns only two responses.
The rebuilt Hyper version completes in 1.2 seconds rather than 0.974 seconds, with all three responses and no long pauses.

edges.comment: Verification of the landed change: the reporter rebuilds and re-measures (c44). Neutral patterns; the mechanism is never named to the user.

satisfaction_conditions: Must identify the root cause: curl's Hyper integration created a new `hyper_clientconn` for each request on a reused HTTP/2 connection, sending repeated HTTP/2 connection prefaces and provoking server GOAWAY/error handling that caused long delays or dropped requests.

The diagnosis must be grounded in the collected trace, packet capture, and protocol comparison: two roughly 30-second idle periods, repeated HTTP/2 prefaces, and fast completion when forcing HTTP/1.1.
The practical fix must disable HTTP/2 for the Hyper backend and fall back to HTTP/1.1 until the Hyper client/executor lifecycle can be redesigned for connection-scoped multiplexing.
Must not present PR #11344's polling changes as the resolution; they were tested in-case and the reporter still observed a roughly 61-second runtime and missing output.
Must require user verification on a rebuilt fixed version, with all three requests completing without the long pauses, before declaring the issue resolved.

persona_hint.experience_level: Experienced curl builder and command-line user who compiles development versions with multiple TLS backends and Hyper, can update Rust toolchains, rebuild dependencies, add debug logging, and provide precise timings; deeper Hyper lifecycle internals are outside the reporter's expertise. Other highly technical affected contributors are folded into the same simulated user side for traces and packet captures.
persona_hint.communication_style: Direct and evidence-driven; supplies reproducible scripts, version output, logs, and benchmark comparisons, while candidly saying when internal implementation details are unfamiliar.
